categories.title: Vocal Training
categories.subtitle: Tone, placement, control, and transitions
categories.description: Core vocal technique drills for stable and expressive singing.

exercises.name: Resonance Placement
exercises.description: Place tone forward while keeping neck and jaw relaxed.
exercises.objective: Practice a stable, forward-feeling tone without adding throat tension.
exercises.what_you_do: Hum and sustain light notes while keeping the tone bright, relaxed, and easy to observe.
instructions: Sustain open vowels with an even, comfortable tone.
Keep tone bright without throat squeeze.
exercises.ai_focus: Tone consistency, projection efficiency, and resonance stability
training_basis: Humming and other semi-occluded vocal-tract exercises are used as gentle warm-up and coordination tasks.
Sustained vowels make pitch steadiness and repeatable tone easier to observe.
measurement_plan: Fundamental frequency (pitch) error in cents against each target note.
Voiced coverage, onset delay, pitch settling time, and pitch variation per target.
Relative loudness consistency and additional microphone acoustic descriptors when available.
measurement_limits: A phone microphone cannot directly measure vocal-tract resonance, throat tension, or airflow.
Resonance and breath-control feedback is an acoustic proxy, not a clinical voice assessment.

coach_cues.ready: Keep the tone forward and the throat easy.
coach_cues.too_soft: Use a clear, comfortable sound without pushing the throat.
coach_cues.on_pitch: Bright and steady - keep the buzz forward.
coach_cues.low_pitch: Lift resonance slightly without adding tension.
coach_cues.high_pitch: Release jaw pressure and let the tone settle.

exercises.name: Pitch Warmup
exercises.description: Warm the voice with controlled pitch center and gentle onset.
exercises.objective: Center the voice with clean onsets and stable pitch in a gentle warmup.
exercises.what_you_do: Sing a short note ladder softly, landing each note cleanly before moving to the next one.
instructions: Hold each target note for 2-3 seconds.
exercises.ai_focus: Pitch center, onset consistency, and warmup control
training_basis: Gentle, progressively wider pitch patterns are a practical way to prepare pitch coordination without forcing volume.
Short repeated targets provide immediate external feedback while keeping practice blocks repeatable.
measurement_plan: Pitch error in cents, target-note coverage, and confident voiced-frame coverage.
Onset delay, pitch settling time, pitch variability, and loudness consistency per note.
measurement_limits: This does not verify vocal-fold health, range safety, or absence of strain.
The pitch detector can be less reliable with noise, breathy tone, very low volume, or overlapping sound.

exercises.name: Note Transition Drill
exercises.description: Improve smooth movement between adjacent target notes.
exercises.objective: Connect notes with controlled transitions and fast pitch settling.
exercises.what_you_do: Sing connected note changes without scooping, dragging, or jumping too hard between pitches.
instructions: Keep the phrase connection even during transitions.
exercises.ai_focus: Transition smoothness, settling speed, and stability
training_basis: Adjacent-note legato work isolates the coordination needed to move between pitches without an uncontrolled slide.
Progressing from steps to a wider octave exposes both small transitions and larger register changes.
measurement_plan: Target-to-target interval, onset delay, pitch settling time, and cents error after each transition.
Completed versus failed transitions, voiced coverage, and pitch stability for each target window.
measurement_limits: The app estimates acoustic pitch movement; it does not see laryngeal motion or diagnose vocal tension.
Transition scores need calibrated recordings before they should be interpreted as a proficiency grade.

coach_cues.on_pitch: Smooth landing - keep the line connected.
coach_cues.low_pitch: Prepare the next note earlier and guide upward.
coach_cues.high_pitch: Release the jump and settle through the breath.

exercises.name: Basic Ladder
exercises.description: Step through scale tones with clean pitch locks.
exercises.objective: Build scale awareness and clean pitch locks on simple note ladders.
exercises.what_you_do: Sing one target note at a time in order, matching each step before climbing to the next one.
instructions: Hold each note until it stabilizes.
exercises.ai_focus: Cents error reduction and note-hit consistency
training_basis: Movable-do solfège links scale-degree hearing to the voice; Do–Sol is a useful beginner pentachord before the full octave.
Intermediate and advanced levels add La, Ti, and high Do so the progression does not stop at Sol.
measurement_plan: Per-note cents error, on-target rate, onset timing, settling time, and pitch stability.
Coverage and confidence are reported so a missing or noisy recording cannot look like a perfect score.
measurement_limits: The drill measures matching to the selected tonic and target notes; it does not prove aural skill outside this pattern.
A numeric score is an engineering measure and still needs human-rated calibration for proficiency claims.

exercises.name: Interval Jumps
exercises.objective: Improve interval anticipation and direct note landing.
exercises.what_you_do: Hear the next note in your mind, then jump directly to it without sliding into the pitch.
instructions: Visualize the target note before singing.
exercises.ai_focus: Interval landing precision and recovery speed
training_basis: Non-adjacent scale-degree jumps train anticipation and direct landing rather than relying only on stepwise sliding.
The advanced pattern samples La, Ti, and high Do so interval work covers the full octave.
measurement_plan: Interval size, landing error in cents, onset delay, settling time, and post-landing stability.
Transition completion rate and recovery time after each guided jump.
measurement_limits: The detector cannot determine whether a singer internally heard the note before singing it.
Large jumps can exceed the configured vocal range; practice range must remain comfortable for the singer.

coach_cues.low_pitch: Prepare the leap higher in your mind.
coach_cues.high_pitch: Release the jump and land with less force.

categories.title: Breathing
categories.subtitle: Breath pacing, body awareness, and phrase endurance
categories.description: Develop breath management for sustained and stable singing.

exercises.name: Support Ladder
exercises.description: Follow guided inhale and exhale counts to practice repeatable breath pacing.
exercises.objective: Practice repeatable breath timing through gradually longer inhale and exhale cycles.
exercises.what_you_do: Follow the timer to inhale, hold briefly if prompted, and exhale slowly through each guided cycle.
instructions: Exhale at steady pressure for the full count.
Keep shoulders relaxed while the timer guides you.
exercises.ai_focus: Breath pacing, routine consistency, and phase completion quality
training_basis: Paced inhale, settle, and exhale phases build repeatable breath timing and body-awareness habits.
The routine is a coordination exercise, not a claim that one breathing pattern fits every singer.
measurement_plan: Phase completion, interruptions, elapsed duration, and consistency of following the guided sequence.
Optional microphone audio proxy: audible-frame coverage, loudness trend, and stream quality.
measurement_limits: A phone microphone cannot measure airflow, lung volume, rib movement, subglottal pressure, or true breath support.
Audio evidence is optional and cannot replace respiratory or airflow sensors.

coach_cues.ready: Set the ribs low and get ready to follow the next breath phase.
coach_cues.too_soft: Keep the exhale even all the way through the release.
coach_cues.on_pitch: Nice pacing - keep the inhale quiet and the exhale even.
coach_cues.low_pitch: Take a fuller, calmer inhale before the next release.
coach_cues.high_pitch: Slow the air down and soften the pressure on the exhale.

beginner.summary: Short guided breathing ladder with simple inhale and longer exhale pacing.
beginner.teaching_note: This is a breathing exercise: follow the inhale and exhale phases instead of singing a note sequence.

stages.title: Inhale
stages.instruction: Breathe in quietly through the nose for the full count.

stages.title: Settle
stages.instruction: Pause briefly and stay relaxed through the ribs.

stages.title: Exhale
stages.instruction: Release the air slowly and evenly until the timer ends.

intermediate.summary: Medium breathing ladder with longer exhale pacing and posture control.
intermediate.teaching_note: This is a breathing exercise: follow the inhale and exhale phases instead of singing a note sequence.

stages.title: Inhale
stages.instruction: Fill low and wide without lifting the shoulders.

stages.title: Anchor
stages.instruction: Keep the ribs open and avoid throat tension.

stages.title: Exhale
stages.instruction: Let the air out in a slow, controlled stream.

stages.title: Recover
stages.instruction: Stay tall and reset calmly before the next cycle.

advanced.summary: Long guided breathing cycle for advanced support pacing and controlled release.
advanced.teaching_note: This is a breathing exercise: follow the inhale and exhale phases instead of singing a note sequence.

stages.instruction: Take a low, silent inhale without rushing.

stages.title: Hold
stages.instruction: Keep the body expanded and steady.

stages.instruction: Release the air with the same support all the way through.

stages.title: Reset
stages.instruction: Relax, recover, and prepare for the next cycle.

exercises.name: Long Phrase Breathing
exercises.description: Practice longer inhale-to-exhale cycles that mimic the pacing needed for long singing phrases.
exercises.objective: Improve phrase planning and exhale pacing through guided long-breath timing.
exercises.what_you_do: Use the timer to inhale, then stretch a calm, even exhale for longer phrase-style counts.
instructions: Pace the exhale instead of pushing air out early.
Stay relaxed until the end of the count.
exercises.ai_focus: Exhale pacing, endurance, and guided phrase completion
training_basis: Longer paced exhale phases rehearse planning and endurance for phrase-length timing.
Professional breathing is variable; the routine is a repeatable practice target, not a universal physiological prescription.
measurement_plan: Phase completion, interruption count, time spent in each guided phase, and cycle consistency.
Optional microphone audio proxy: audible-frame coverage, loudness trend, and stream quality.
measurement_limits: A phone microphone cannot prove airflow pacing or respiratory kinematics.
Stop if dizzy, uncomfortable, or strained; this app is not medical or respiratory therapy.

coach_cues.ready: Plan the breath now and stay calm through the longer release.
coach_cues.too_soft: Keep the support connected as the phrase keeps going.
coach_cues.on_pitch: That pacing is steady - keep the exhale smooth to the end.
coach_cues.low_pitch: Reset calmly so the next long release stays comfortable.
coach_cues.high_pitch: Back off the pressure and spread the air across the full phrase.

beginner.summary: Short phrase-style breathing cycle with a measured inhale and longer exhale.
beginner.teaching_note: This is a breathing exercise: follow the inhale and exhale phases instead of singing a note sequence.

stages.title: Finish

stages.instruction: Release tension and prepare for the next cycle.
